coverage: Generator VALIDATION coverage: 19 generators x 8 seeds x 2000 draws vs real libraries, all PASS. Space MEASURED: bash $RANDOM is one orbit per implementation variant (seed IS the state, brand() is a pure map), so seed and keystream-offset are the SAME AXIS for that family; bash4.2 LP64 cycle 2^31-2 (tail 13-72), bash4.2_i32 cycle 343,896 (tail 210k-500k); the auto-seeded path (sbrand(tv_sec ^ tv_usec ^ getpid), variables.c:537) reaches at most 74 * 2^20 = 77,594,624 seeds for a 2012-01..2014-06 run, i.e. 3.6% of 2^31, which is a PRIORITY ORDERING inside the full range. glibc seed space 2^32-1 with no orbit collapse (state 31x32 bits). Measured throughput: 166 beam decodes/s/core (I3 vecbeam), 55 end-to-end with I1+I2, 137,414 rows/s/core for a rigid L=31 9-register head-window screen.
not_covered: NO KEYSTREAM WAS SCORED AGAINST LP2. Phase 0 hold, by design.
bash4.2_i32 has no L1 reference: gcc-multilib absent, so no real 32-bit bash 4.2 binary. The ILP32 model is the same source re-typed with uint32_t/int32_t (level L4).

shuf --random-source is validated against GNU coreutils 9.7, NOT the 8.13 of Ubuntu 12.04; randint_genmax byte-consumption may have changed. Ubuntu 26.04 also ships the Rust uutils shuf as /usr/bin/shuf; G1 prefers /usr/bin/gnushuf.

bash3.2 LP64 orbit is stated analytically, not measured: its map is a full-period LCG mod 2^64 (Hull-Dobell), so Brent would need 2^64 evaluations; the 15-bit output period is 2^31 by the bit-period argument, and the ILP32 sibling measures exactly 2^32 as predicted. Every other bash variant's orbit IS measured (see control_detail.G1-ORB).

bash 4.0/4.1 are only PARTIALLY enumerable: seedrand() re-seeds from gettimeofday^getpid when the state reaches 0, and state 0 IS reachable (RANDOM=2147483647 reaches it in one step). Only the deterministic prefix exists.
openssl enc -k overlaps LEDGER R16-KDF (692,064 configs); the overlap was not computed and S1 must de-duplicate.

lrand48 and Perl-drand48 are round10/L5-seed32/CENSUS.md section B generators 10 and 11, already covered over 2011-2015 unix-seconds; G1 re-implements them only for interface uniformity and S1 must NOT re-sweep that window.
/dev/urandom, bare shuf, `openssl rand`, and bash 5.1's $SRANDOM are UNREACHABLE -- no seed and no record. Not swept, and NO NULL IS REPORTED for them.
The auto-seeded 77.6M subset is an upper bound on the seed SET; the joint distribution of (tv_sec, tv_usec, pid) was not modelled, so the subset cannot yet be ordered by likelihood.

notes: THREE CORRECTIONS THIS LANE MADE TO THE REPO'S OWN FRAMING. (1) round18/L1-toolchain RESULTS.md section 6.2 row 4 describes $RANDOM as 'a 15-bit glibc rand() derivative'. It is not, in any bash release: bash 3.2 uses its own LCG and bash 4.0-5.2 their own Park-Miller/Schrage generator in variables.c / lib/sh/random.c. $RANDOM never calls libc rand(). The PRIOR stands; the mechanism claim does not, and $RANDOM must be swept as an independent generator. (2) 'openssl rand with a short passphrase' does not name a real command -- no OpenSSL 1.0.x gives `rand` a seed or passphrase option; the real object with that shape is `openssl enc -k`. (3) A naive reading of bash 4.2 suggests a script that never assigns RANDOM starts deterministically from rseed=1; it does NOT -- initialize_shell_variables() calls seedrand() at variables.c:537. Reading the source killed that hypothesis before it cost anything. ALSO: bash's $RANDOM has ALWAYS wrapped brand() in `do rv = brand(); while (rv == last_random_value);` -- a rejection loop in the standard library of the shell L1 puts on the author's box. At 15-bit granularity it suppresses ~1/32768 of draws and CANNOT produce LP2's mod-29 doublet deficit (0.664% vs 3.45% expected). Recorded as a shape-match only; it is NOT offered as evidence.
